Only my file exists, and the full suite run above (`Tests run: 26, Failures: 2`) already covers it completely, with `compiled OK`. The test class is complete and ready.

## Summary

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest.java` with 26 JUnit 4 tests covering construction, locale handling, custom-format registry behavior, format-element parsing edge cases, disabled mutators, quoting, and error cases.

24 tests pass. 2 tests fail, and both point to real bugs in `ExtendedMessageFormat`:

1. **`testWhitespaceAroundFormatElementIsTrimmed`** — exposes that `parseFormatDescription` only strips *leading* whitespace from a format name/style (via `seekNonWs` at the start), but never strips *trailing* whitespace before the closing `}` (or before a `,`). For a pattern like `"{ 0 , upper }"`, the parsed format name ends up as `"upper "` (trailing space), the registry lookup for `"upper"` fails, and the leftover `,upper ` is handed to the base `java.text.MessageFormat`, which blows up with `IllegalArgumentException: unknown format type: upper`. This directly contradicts the class's own Javadoc: "format-name and format-style values are trimmed of surrounding whitespace in the manner of `java.text.MessageFormat`."

2. **`testQuotedLiteralBraceBeforeCustomFormatElement`** — exposes a crash when a quoted literal brace (e.g. `'{0}'`) appears before a real registry-backed custom format element, e.g. pattern `"'{0}' {1,upper}"`. `applyPattern` itself succeeds, but `toPattern()`'s reconstruction via `insertFormats` re-scans `super.toPattern()`'s own canonical (re-quoted) output using the same fragile index-parsing logic, and that mismatch causes `readArgumentIndex` to hit a quote character where it expects a digit, throwing `IllegalArgumentException: Invalid format argument index at position 2: '`. Root cause traces back to `appendQuotedString`'s escaped-quote shortcut (`if (escapingOn && c[start] == QUOTE) { ... }`), which fires on every single quote rather than only on a doubled `''`, so quoted sections are never actually skipped as literal blocks by the custom-format bookkeeping — it just happens to usually still work when nothing follows the quoted section.
